stats.label: Time to regain focus after an email interruption

blocks.text: Why Gmail is the standard for PR managers

Public relations managers deal with high volumes of incoming messages. You need a tool that handles search, threads and labels without slowing down. Gmail provides this through its web interface. It does not have a native Mac app, but you can create one. Open Chrome or Safari and look for the option to install as a web app. This places a Gmail icon in your Dock. It keeps your email separate from your research tabs.

You should not use your mouse for every action. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts. Turn them on to save time. Press ? at any time to see the full list. Use j and k to move through threads. Press e to archive. Press r to reply. These small changes add up over a long day of pitching.

PR managers often send personalized pitches to many journalists. Gmail has a daily sending limit of 500 recipients for personal accounts and 2,000 for Workspace. Keep your lists clean. Use labels to track which journalists have responded. Create a filter to move emails from specific domains into dedicated folders. This prevents your primary inbox from getting cluttered with automated press releases or monitoring alerts.

Lazur helps you stay in the flow. When you are stuck on a complex email, hold the ⌥ ⌘ keys. Ask Lazur to summarize a long thread. It will read the screen and give you the key points. If you need to write a quick response, hold the fn key to dictate your thoughts. Lazur turns your speech into clean text at the cursor.

items: Ignoring the keyboard shortcut settings in the menu.
Keeping too many browser tabs open for different email accounts.
Failing to use labels for urgent client requests.
Sending attachments that exceed size limits without checking.
Forgetting to use the Undo Send feature after hitting enter.

blocks.text: A cluttered inbox ruins your concentration. Use the search bar to find emails with specific attachments. Use the advanced search operators to filter by date or sender. If you find yourself checking email every few minutes, set a timer. Block out time for deep work. Use Lazur to set a reminder for when to check your inbox again. This helps you protect your focus during critical campaign periods.

PR managers often send large files. Gmail allows attachments up to 25 MB. For larger files, use Google Drive and insert the link. Do not clutter your email with heavy files. If you need to track when a client opens a report, use a CRM tool that integrates with Gmail. Keep your communication professional and concise.

items: Use the snooze feature to deal with non-urgent emails later.
Create a canned response for common journalist queries.
Set up an out of office reply when you are at a media event.
Use delegate access if you have an assistant helping with your inbox.
Mute conversations that are no longer relevant to your current project.

blocks.text: Your Mac is a powerful tool. Use Spotlight by pressing ⌘ + Space to open Gmail or your other apps. Keep your desktop clean. Use virtual desktops to separate your PR work from your personal tasks. Control + Left or Right arrow lets you switch between them. This helps you maintain a clear boundary between your creative work and your administrative duties.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native desktop app for Gmail. You can create a web app using Safari or Chrome to get a similar experience.

faq.question: How do I make Gmail faster on Mac?
faq.answer: Enable keyboard shortcuts in your Gmail settings. Use the web app version to keep your email isolated from other browser tabs.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me with my emails?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur to summarize emails on your screen. Hold fn to dictate your replies directly into the compose window.

faq.question: What is the daily sending limit for Gmail?
faq.answer: Personal accounts can send to 500 recipients per day. Workspace accounts can send to 2,000 recipients per day.
